title: Assumption Hygiene — assumption–guarantee boundary, four predicates, vacuity detection; 'assume only what the environment guarantees'

source.source_reference: Shawn's explicit teaching, main chat, 2026-10-10. Filed same-evening per his standing law: his word IS the verification (Verification Law); filed immediately, not queued.

intelligence.essence: A model checker can report success while the scheduler starves — if the proof assumes what it was supposed to prove. The assumption–guarantee boundary: the environment gets only assumptions it can independently guarantee (e.g., resource availability under defined conditions); the scheduler's selection, service, and fairness are PROPERTIES TO PROVE, never assumptions. Four predicates prevent circular eligibility: OUTSTANDING (needs resolution), ADMISSIBLE (authority permits), READY (everything but scheduling), ENABLED (a real transition can occur) — eligibility is never defined as 'already chosen by the scheduler.' Every assumption gets an eight-question audit (who controls it, can it hide a counterexample, is it satisfiable, does it already imply the result...). Three models run: adversarial (hunt starvation), justified (prove without assuming fairness), runtime refinement (the real scheduler obeys the model). Vacuity detection rejects proofs about empty worlds: assumption satisfiability, enablement witnesses, and the mutation test — a deliberately broken scheduler must FAIL, or the proof configuration itself is suspect. Verdicts: PROVED_IN_SCOPE, VACUOUS, ASSUMPTIONS_UNJUSTIFIED, COUNTEREXAMPLE_FOUND, UNKNOWN. The rule: 'No fairness qualification is accepted unless its environmental assumptions are explicit, independently justified, satisfiable, minimally sufficient, and tested against known scheduler defects.'

human_view.meaning: Never let the proof assume the conclusion. The environment gets assumptions it can actually back up; everything the scheduler is supposed to do must be PROVEN, not assumed. And if the proof's world is so rigged that nothing could fail in it, the proof is worthless — we check for that automatically.
human_view.why_it_matters: This is the integrity check on verification itself. Every proof in the stack is only as honest as its assumptions; this law audits the auditors.

naya_view.directive: Draw the assumption–guarantee boundary on every liveness proof. Use the four predicates; never define eligibility as scheduler choice. Audit every assumption with the eight questions; run the three models; run the vacuity checks including the broken-scheduler mutation test. Reject VACUOUS and ASSUMPTIONS_UNJUSTIFIED as qualifications.

ai_view.specification: A_env ∧ I_sched ⊨ F_sched (F_sched NOT assumed). Predicates: OUTSTANDING/ADMISSIBLE/READY/ENABLED. Audit: 8 questions. Models: A (adversarial), B (justified), C (refinement). Vacuity: 6 checks incl. mutation test. Verdicts: 5 states, no collapsed PASS.
ai_view.directive: Follow as written. This is law, not guidance. A VACUOUS proof cited as qualification is a law violation.

intelligence.learning_lesson: Folded into the fairness-verification build 2026-10-10; the smallest experiment (intermittent ACT + starving scheduler + overstrong assumption) is the standing acceptance test.

intelligence.uncertainty: Audit question wording and check implementations are implementer-defined; the boundary, the four predicates, and the mutation test are fixed.
intelligence.applicability: Every seat that writes, runs, or cites a model-checked liveness proof.
intelligence.falsifier: Falsified if a proof assumes its conclusion, or a broken scheduler passes the mutation test.
intelligence.measurement_contract: Track vacuity-check outcomes per proof; every excluded counterexample must name its excluding assumption.
intelligence.successor_effect: A cold successor handed a green model-checking result asks 'what was assumed, what did it exclude, could a broken scheduler still pass' — and rejects the PASS if the answers are bad.
